We actually had a lecture the other day in my media law class about how facebook, for all intents and purposes, is straight up "the internet" for many people, which is pretty alarming, meaning it is the one and only way these people interact online, and thus the filter through which they absorb any and all online content and information... I'm afraid old Zuckerberg already has far too much power as it is.

Normally I'd be against the idea, but Facebook's proven we need "public square" regulations to stop social media behemoths from abusing their influence. The big problems are where to start and how to make sure it doesn't succumb to immediate regulatory capture.

On the one hand, it's great to have that public forum-style interchange of people exchanging information directly with each other, safely outside the filters of mainstream information outlets. On the other hand though, once Facebook starts fucking with what users can and can't see to fit their own agenda, it becomes a huge problem very quickly. I think a lot of people (wrongly) assume their first amendment rights carry over to a private company like Facebook, whereas we know, of course, that it can quite happily dictate and control exactly what information people can see or talk about to a scary, 1984-level degree.

As more and more people around the world start channeling any and all information and communication through things like facebook and twitter, the power of these companies to shape the public, perceived narrative in the way they see fit becomes increasingly stronger. What percentage of people communicate only and exclusively these mediums? I'm sure it's growing. As a libertarian, the idea of government stepping in and forcing a private company to allow free speech is obviously problematic, but if and when the vast percentage of people are communicating through these very censor-able mediums, at what point do we start having a problem? Have these companies grown so large and powerful they've transcended and moved beyond the rights of a normal, private company? Is this a case we'd want direct government intervention? Just some thoughts I've been batting around lately.
